newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Strike at Standard Chartered Zimbabwe continues.
newsitem.headline: Strike at Standard Chartered Zimbabwe continues.

text.p: Workers at Standard Chartered Bank Zimbabwe Ltd who went on strike on Wednesday demanding better working conditions continued their stayaway on Thursday.
A senior bank official said bank authorities and the strikers were meeting officials from the labour ministry to try and resolve the dispute which has disrupted banking services.

"Meetings are still being held with workers and the ministry, which will be issuing a disposal order soon," Standard head of corporate affairs Terry McCabe said, refusing to comment further on what had transpired.
He also would not say what action management would take against the strikers but added, "We're not being confrontational with the workers."

The workers accuse management of frustrating their attempts to resolve profit-sharing and performance appraisal problems, which they say have been dragging on since 1995. They have vowed not to return to work until their grievances are addressed.
Their representatives say some 95 percent of non-managerial employees at the bank, which has a national staff compliment of 1,730, are on strike.
McCabe said by the end of business on Wednesday, 70 percent of the bank's branches countrywide were offering "full or limited services" compared to around 50 percent earlier in the day.
The situation was still unchanged on Thursday morning, he added.
